title: We pray only to God, through His Word
source_text: οὔτε πιστευτέον δαίμοσι, κἂν Κέλσος ἐπὶ τούτους ἡμᾶς παρακαλῇ. ἀλλ᾿ ἀποθανητέον πρὶν πεισθῆναι δαίμοσιν ἀλλὰ καὶ πᾶν ὁτιοῦν ὑπομενετέον πειθό μενον θεῷ. οὕτως δὲ οὐδὲ καλλιερητέον δαίμοσι· καὶ γὰρ ἀδύνατόν ἐστι τοῖς φαύλοις καὶ ἀνθρώπων κακωτικοῖς καλλιερεῖν. ἀλλὰ καὶ κατὰ ποίους νόμους ἡμᾶς βούλεται Κέλσος καλλιερεῖν τοῖς δαίμοσιν; εἰ μὲν γὰρ κατὰ τοὺς κειμένους ἐν ταῖς πόλεσι, κατασκευαζέτω ὅτι συνᾴδουσι τοῖς θείοις νόμοις· εἰ δὲ τοῦτο μὴ δύναται (οὐ γὰρ κἂν ἀλλήλοις ταὐτὰ λέγουσιν οἱ τῶν πολλῶν πόλεων νόμοι), δηλονότι οὐδὲ κυρίως νόμους ἢ φαύλων νόμους, οἷς οὐ πιστευτέον· „πειθαρχεῖν“ γὰρ „δεῖ μᾶλλον θεῷ ἢ ἀνθρώποις.“ ἄπαγε δὴ τὴν τοῦ Κέλσου συμβουλὴν, λέγοντος προσευκτέον εἶναι δαίμοσι, καὶ οὐδὲ κατὰ τὸ ποσὸν ἀκουστέον αὐτῆς· μόνῳ γὰρ προσευκτέον τῷ ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεῷ, καὶ προσευκτέον γε τῷ μονογενεῖ καὶ πρωτοτόκῳ „πάσης κτίσεως“ λόγῳ θεοῦ. καὶ ἀξιωτέον αὐτὸν ὡς ἀρχιερέα τὴν ἐπ᾿ αὐτὸν φθάσασαν ἡμῶν εὐχὴν ἀναφέρειν ἐπὶ τὸν θεὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ θεὸν ἡμῶν καὶ πατέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ πατέρα τῶν βιούντων κατὰ τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ. ὥσπερ δὲ οὐκ ἂν βουλοίμεθα εὐμενεῖς ἔχειν ἀνθρώπους τοὺς βουλομένους ἡμᾶς βιοῦν κατὰ τὴν αὐτῶν κακίαν. ἐὰν μηδενὶ τυγχάνωσιν ὄντες εὐμενεῖς τῶν τὰ ἐναντία αὐτοῖς αἱρουμένων. ἐπεὶ ἡ εὐμένεια αὐτῶν ἐχθροὺς ἡμᾶς ποιεῖ θεῷ. τάχα μὴ γινομένῳ εὐμενεῖ τοῖς θέλουσι τοὺς τοιούτους ἔχειν εὐμενεῖς· τὸν αὐτὸν τρόπον οἱ νοήσαντες δαιμόνων φύσιν καὶ προαίρεσιν καὶ κακίαν οὐκ ἄν ποτε βούλοιντο εὐμενεῖς ἔχειν τοὺς δαίμονας.
pass_a_gloss: Nor must one trust (πιστευτέον) demons, even if Celsus calls (παρακαλῇ) us to them; but one must die (ἀποθανητέον) before being persuaded by (πεισθῆναι) demons, and must endure (ὑπομενετέον) anything whatever obeying (πειθόμενον) God. So neither must one sacrifice with good omens (καλλιερητέον) to demons; for it is impossible to sacrifice with good omens to the base (φαῦλοι) and harmful to men (κακωτικοί). And according to what sort of laws does Celsus want us to sacrifice to the demons? If according to those laid down (κειμένους) in the cities (πόλεις), let him establish (κατασκευαζέτω) that they accord (συνᾴδουσι) with the divine laws; but if he cannot (for the laws of the many cities do not even say the same things to one another), clearly they are not laws properly (κυρίως), or laws of the base, which one must not trust; for 'one must obey (πειθαρχεῖν) God rather than men'. Away (ἄπαγε) with the counsel (συμβουλή) of Celsus, saying one must pray to demons, and one must not listen to it even in quantity (κατὰ τὸ ποσόν); for one must pray to the God over all (ὁ ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεός) alone, and one must pray also to the only-begotten (μονογενής) and firstborn (πρωτότοκος) 'of all creation (κτίσις)' Word of God. And one must ask (ἀξιωτέον) Him, as high priest (ἀρχιερεύς), to carry up (ἀναφέρειν) our prayer (εὐχή) which has reached (φθάσασαν) Him to His God and our God and His Father and Father of those living (βιούντων) according to the Word of God. As we would not wish to have well-disposed men who want us to live according to their wickedness, if they are well-disposed to none of those choosing (αἱρουμένων) the opposite, since their goodwill (εὐμένεια) makes us enemies (ἐχθροί) to God, perhaps (τάχα) not becoming well-disposed to those wishing to have such well-disposed; in the same way those who have understood the nature (φύσις), purpose (προαίρεσις) and wickedness (κακία) of demons would never wish to have the demons well-disposed.
pass_b_english: Nor must we put our trust in demons, even if Celsus urges us toward them. Instead, we must die rather than obey demons, and endure anything whatever in obeying God. In the same way we must not offer acceptable sacrifices to demons, for it is impossible to offer acceptable sacrifices to beings that are wicked and do harm to men.

And according to what laws does Celsus want us to offer acceptable sacrifices to the demons? If according to the laws established in the cities, let him prove that they agree with the divine laws. But if he cannot do this (for the laws of the many cities do not even agree with one another), then clearly they are either not laws in the proper sense, or laws of wicked men, which we must not trust; for “we must obey God rather than men” (Acts 5:29).

Away, then, with the counsel of Celsus, who says that we must pray to demons; we must not listen to it even in the least. For we must pray to the God over all, and to Him alone; and indeed we must pray also to the only-begotten Word of God, “the firstborn of all creation” (Colossians 1:15). And we must ask Him, as High Priest (Hebrews 4:14), to carry up our prayer, once it has reached Him, to His God and our God, and to His Father and the Father of those who live according to the Word of God (John 20:17).

Just as we would not wish to have men well disposed toward us who want us to live according to their own wickedness, if they are well disposed to none of those who choose the opposite course, since their goodwill makes us enemies of God, who perhaps does not become well disposed to those who wish to have such men well disposed toward them; in the same way, those who have understood the nature of demons, their will, and their wickedness would never wish to have the demons well disposed.

choices.choice: The chapter opens with the second half of the ‘neither ... nor’ sentence begun at the end of chapter 25. πιστευτέον is rendered ‘put our trust in’ / ‘trust’ to match Celsus’s word in chapter 24. ἀποθανητέον πρὶν πεισθῆναι δαίμοσιν: πρίν here gives preference (‘die rather than obey’), not a sequence in time. The sentence on the cities’ laws is elliptical (δηλονότι οὐδὲ κυρίως νόμους ἢ φαύλων νόμους); ‘they are either not laws in the proper sense, or laws of wicked men’ supplies the verb. Acts 5:29 is quoted with πειθαρχεῖν δεῖ μᾶλλον θεῷ. On prayer: Origen says prayer is to be made ‘to the God over all alone’ (μόνῳ) and also (καὶ ... γε) to the only-begotten Word, whom we ask as High Priest to carry our prayer to the Father; both clauses are kept exactly as he gives them. The quotation marks for Colossians 1:15 take in ‘firstborn’ (πρωτοτόκῳ πάσης κτίσεως is the verse’s phrase), although the edition marks only πάσης κτίσεως. ‘High Priest’ is cited as an allusion to Hebrews 4:14 (compare Hebrews 7:25 for intercession); the sequence ‘His God and our God ... His Father and the Father’ alludes to John 20:17. The final sentence keeps Origen’s ὥσπερ ... τὸν αὐτὸν τρόπον (‘Just as ... in the same way’) frame. ‘Who perhaps does not become well disposed’ keeps Origen’s τάχα (‘perhaps’).
'we must die before we obey demons' to 'we must die rather than obey demons' (πρίν of preference, not time)
'do not even say the same things as one another' to 'do not even agree with one another' (calque)
'pray to the God over all alone' (ambiguous English order) to 'pray to the God over all, and to Him alone'; 'also' to 'indeed ... also' (καὶ ... γε)
Colossians 1:15 quotation marks extended to 'the firstborn of all creation'
Restored the missing 'Just as' (ὥσπερ) that pairs with 'in the same way', and joined the two halves into one comparison
